lpic1-ficheros.title: Organizing a downloads folder
lpic1-ficheros.briefing:
The `descargas/` folder has mixed files. Leave it like this:
1. Create the folders `descargas/logs` and `descargas/fotos`.
2. Move all `*.log` to `logs/` and all `*.jpg` to `fotos/` (none may remain outside).
3. Delete all `*.tmp`.
4. Copy `informe.txt` as `informe.txt.bak` in the same folder.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-ficheros`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-ficheros.blind_alert: REQUEST [ORDER] · A downloads folder needs to be reorganized by file type and temporary files cleaned up.
hints: This is about creating, moving, deleting, and copying with wildcards so you don't go file by file.
`mkdir -p` creates directories, `mv *.log logs/` moves by pattern, `rm *.tmp` deletes by pattern, and `cp origen destino` copies. Work inside `descargas/`.
`cd descargas`; `mkdir -p logs fotos`; `mv *.log logs/`; `mv *.jpg fotos/`; `rm *.tmp`; `cp informe.txt informe.txt.bak`.
lpic1-ficheros.solution_summary: `mkdir`, `mv`, `rm`, and `cp` with wildcards (`*.log`, `*.jpg`, `*.tmp`) reorganize the files in bulk; `cp informe.txt informe.txt.bak` leaves an identical copy next to the original.

informe.txt.bak is a copy of informe.txt

lpic1-filtros.title: Extracting data from a CSV with filters
lpic1-filtros.briefing:
`ventas.csv` has lines `ciudad,producto,unidades` (no header). Generate:
1. `ciudades.txt`, with the distinct cities sorted alphabetically, one per line.
2. `madrid.txt`, with only the Madrid lines, exactly as they appear in the original.
3. `cuantas.txt`, with the number of lines in `ventas.csv` (just the number, without the filename).
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-filtros`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-filtros.blind_alert: REQUEST [REPORTS] · Three summaries need to be extracted from a sales CSV file.
hints: Each result is obtained by chaining text filters: cut a field, sort without duplicates, select lines, and count them.
`cut -d, -f1` gets the first field and `sort -u` sorts without duplicates; `grep '^Madrid,'` filters by start of line; `wc -l < fichero` counts without printing the name.
`cut -d, -f1 ventas.csv | sort -u > ciudades.txt`; `grep '^Madrid,' ventas.csv > madrid.txt`; `wc -l < ventas.csv > cuantas.txt`.
lpic1-filtros.solution_summary: `cut -d, -f1 | sort -u` extracts and sorts the distinct values of a column, `grep '^Madrid,'` selects by start-of-line pattern, and `wc -l < fichero` counts lines without printing the name.

checks.ciudades.txt: las ciudades distintas, or: ciudades.txt: the distinct cities, sorted, one per line
checks.cuantas.txt: el número de líneas de vent: cuantas.txt: the number of lines in ventas.csv

lpic1-redirecciones.title: Separating normal output from errors
lpic1-redirecciones.briefing:
The `./genera.sh` script writes normal lines (stdout) and error lines (stderr). You need to:
1. Run it, in a single command, saving the normal output to `salida.txt` and the errors to `errores.txt`.
2. Append the current date from `date` to the end of `salida.txt` without erasing what's already there.
3. Create `mayus.txt` with the contents of `salida.txt` in uppercase, using a pipe and `tr`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-redirecciones`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-redirecciones.blind_alert: REQUEST [PROCESSING] · The errors from a script need to be separated from its normal output and an uppercase copy generated.
hints: There are two output streams, each with its own descriptor number, and both can be redirected at once in the same command. Appending without overwriting requires a different operator.
`>` for stdout, `2>` for stderr, `>>` to append; the pipe `|` connects the output of `cat` to `tr a-z A-Z`.
`./genera.sh > salida.txt 2> errores.txt`; `date >> salida.txt`; `cat salida.txt | tr a-z A-Z > mayus.txt`.
lpic1-redirecciones.solution_summary: `> fichero` redirects stdout and `2> fichero` redirects stderr; `>>` appends without truncating; with `cat salida.txt | tr a-z A-Z`, the pipe passes the text to `tr`, which converts it to uppercase.

checks.salida.txt: la salida normal del script: salida.txt: the normal output of the script
checks.salida.txt: lleva una línea añadida al f: salida.txt: has an appended line at the end

lpic1-grep.title: Searching a log with regular expressions
lpic1-grep.briefing:
`acceso.log` is the log of a web server (each line: IP, method, path, and response code as the last field). Generate:
1. `internas.txt`, with the lines whose IP starts with `192.168.` (watch out for addresses that look similar but don't start that way).
2. `fallos.txt`, with the lines whose response code is 404 or 500.
3. `n-post.txt`, with the number of lines containing `POST` (just the number).
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-grep`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-grep.blind_alert: REQUEST [SEARCH] · The internal requests, the errors, and the count of POST submissions need to be extracted from a web server log.
hints: Line-start and line-end anchors matter here, as well as escaping the dot (which in a regular expression means “any character”), and the difference between displaying lines and counting them.
`grep '^192\.168\.'` anchors to the start and escapes the dots; `grep -E ' (404|500)$'` uses alternation at the end of the line; `grep -c` counts the matching lines.
`grep '^192\.168\.' acceso.log > internas.txt`; `grep -E ' (404|500)$' acceso.log > fallos.txt`; `grep -c POST acceso.log > n-post.txt`.
lpic1-grep.solution_summary: `^` anchors to the start of the line and `\.` represents a literal dot, so the lookalike IP is discarded; `-E` enables the alternation `(404|500)` and `$` fixes the end; `grep -c` returns how many lines match instead of showing them.

checks.internas.txt: las líneas cuya IP empieza: internas.txt: the lines whose IP starts with 192.168. (and only those)
checks.fallos.txt: las líneas con código 404 o: fallos.txt: the lines with code 404 or 500
checks.n-post.txt: el número de líneas con POST: n-post.txt: the number of lines with POST

lpic1-permisos.title: Numeric permissions, SGID, and sticky bit
lpic1-permisos.briefing:
You are asked to leave these permissions (for the group you need `sudo`):
1. `secreto.txt` with permissions 600 (only the owner reads and writes).
2. `script.sh` with 744: `rwx` for the owner and read-only for group and others.
3. Create the group `proyecto`, make the `compartida/` folder belong to that group, and give it 2775 (SGID: new items inside inherit the group).
4. The `publica/` folder must have the sticky bit with permissions 1777, like `/tmp`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-permisos`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-permisos.blind_alert: REQUEST [PERMISSIONS] · A secret, a script, and two shared folders need to be left with the correct special permissions.
hints: Permissions are written in octal; the special bits (SGID, sticky) go in a fourth digit in front. Creating a group and changing a folder's ownership requires privileges.
`chmod 600`, `chmod 744`; `groupadd`, `chgrp GRUPO carpeta`, and `chmod 2775`; `chmod 1777` (or `chmod +t`).
`chmod 600 secreto.txt`; `chmod 744 script.sh`; `sudo groupadd proyecto`; `sudo chgrp proyecto compartida`; `chmod 2775 compartida`; `chmod 1777 publica`.
lpic1-permisos.solution_summary: `chmod` in octal sets 600 and 744; `2775` adds SGID (new files inherit the group of the folder) and `1777` adds the sticky bit (only the owner deletes their own files). The group is created with `groupadd` and assigned with `chgrp`, both with privileges.

checks.compartida/ es del grupo proyecto: compartida/ belongs to the group proyecto

lpic1-enlaces.title: Hard and symbolic links
lpic1-enlaces.briefing:
You are asked to create three links:
1. `duro.txt`, as a hard link to `original.txt`.
2. `blando.txt`, as a symbolic link to `original.txt` (the target is the relative name `original.txt`).
3. Inside the `atajos/` folder, a symbolic link called `conf` that points to `/etc/hostname`.
To view them: `ls -li` shows the inode and the link count.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-enlaces`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-enlaces.blind_alert: REQUEST [LINKS] · A file needs to be left accessible under a second name and two shortcuts created.
hints: A hard link is another name for the same inode; a symbolic link is a small file that stores a path. The same command creates both, with an option that tells them apart.
`ln origen destino` makes the hard one; `ln -s origen destino` makes the symbolic one. In a symbolic link, the first argument is the destination path text exactly as given.
`ln original.txt duro.txt`; `ln -s original.txt blando.txt`; `ln -s /etc/hostname atajos/conf`.
lpic1-enlaces.solution_summary: `ln` without options creates a hard link (same inode as the original); `ln -s` creates a symbolic link that stores the target path, which can be relative (`original.txt`) or absolute (`/etc/hostname`).

checks.duro.txt existe y no es un enlace simból: duro.txt exists and is not a symbolic link
checks.duro.txt comparte inodo con original.txt: duro.txt shares an inode with original.txt
checks.blando.txt es simbólico y apunta a origi: blando.txt is symbolic and points to original.txt

lpic1-sistema-archivos.title: An ext4 filesystem inside a file
lpic1-sistema-archivos.briefing:
In a container there are no real disks, so you'll use a file as a disk (`mkfs.ext4`, `tune2fs`, and `blkid` are in `/usr/sbin`: use `sudo`):
1. Create `disco.img` of exactly 64 MiB (67108864 bytes).
2. Format it as ext4 with the label `DATOS`.
3. With `tune2fs`, set the maximum mount count before forcing a check to 30.
4. Save the output of `blkid` applied to `disco.img` in `info.txt`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-sistema-archivos`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-sistema-archivos.blind_alert: REQUEST [STORAGE] · A labeled ext4 volume needs to be prepared, its periodic check adjusted, and documented.
hints: A file works as a block device for `mkfs`, `tune2fs`, and `blkid`. The label is set when formatting, and the mount counter is adjusted afterward.
`truncate -s 64M` creates the file; `sudo mkfs.ext4 -L ETIQUETA fichero` formats; `sudo tune2fs -c N` sets the maximum mount count; `sudo blkid fichero` prints the type and label.
`truncate -s 64M disco.img`; `sudo mkfs.ext4 -L DATOS disco.img`; `sudo tune2fs -c 30 disco.img`; `sudo blkid disco.img > info.txt`.
lpic1-sistema-archivos.solution_summary: `truncate -s 64M` creates the 64 MiB file; `mkfs.ext4 -L DATOS` formats it with a label; `tune2fs -c 30` sets the maximum mount count, and `blkid` shows TYPE and LABEL, which are saved in `info.txt`.

lpic1-dpkg.title: Debian packages: install, list files, and find the owner
lpic1-dpkg.briefing:
The `tree` package is uninstalled. You are asked to (you need `sudo` and internet access; the image doesn't include the package index, so update it before installing):
1. Install `tree` with `apt`.
2. Save the list of files installed by that package, obtained with `dpkg`, in `archivos-tree.txt`.
3. Save the output of `dpkg -S /usr/bin/ls`, which indicates which package that file belongs to, in `duenno.txt`.
Note: in Debian 13 `/bin` is a link to `/usr/bin`, and `dpkg -S /bin/ls` finds nothing because dpkg only knows the path each file was installed with.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-dpkg`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-dpkg.blind_alert: REQUEST [PACKAGES] · A utility needs to be installed and its files documented, along with which package a system command belongs to.
hints: `apt` installs (with `sudo` and an up-to-date index); `dpkg` queries the installed package database, both “which files it brings” and “which package this file belongs to”.
`sudo apt-get update` and `sudo apt install -y tree`; `dpkg -L paquete` lists files; `dpkg -S ruta` finds the owning package (with the exact path under `/usr`).
`sudo apt-get update && sudo apt install -y tree`; `dpkg -L tree > archivos-tree.txt`; `dpkg -S /usr/bin/ls > duenno.txt`.
lpic1-dpkg.solution_summary: `apt install` installs the package after `apt-get update`; `dpkg -L tree` lists its files (including `/usr/bin/tree`) and `dpkg -S /usr/bin/ls` reveals that the owner is `coreutils`. With the unified /usr you must use the path under `/usr`.

checks.archivos-tree.txt: la lista de ficheros: archivos-tree.txt: the list of files from the tree package

lpic1-rpm.title: RPM packages with dnf and rpm (on Fedora)
lpic1-rpm.briefing:
This challenge is done on a Fedora machine (the terminal already is one). The `tree` package is not installed. You need `sudo` and internet access:
1. Install `tree` with `dnf`.
2. Save the package that `/usr/bin/bash` belongs to, queried with `rpm`, in `duenno.txt`.
3. Save the list of files from the `tree` package, obtained with `rpm`, in `archivos-tree.txt`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-rpm`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-rpm.blind_alert: REQUEST [PACKAGES] · A utility needs to be installed on Fedora and its contents documented, along with the package of a base command.
hints: `dnf` manages repositories and installations; `rpm` queries the local package database with query options (`-q`).
`sudo dnf install -y tree`; `rpm -qf RUTA` says which package a file belongs to; `rpm -ql PAQUETE` lists its files.
`sudo dnf install -y tree`; `rpm -qf /usr/bin/bash > duenno.txt`; `rpm -ql tree > archivos-tree.txt`.
lpic1-rpm.solution_summary: `dnf install` installs from the repositories; `rpm -qf /usr/bin/bash` returns the owning package (`bash-…`) and `rpm -ql tree` lists the files the package brings, including `/usr/bin/tree`.

checks.archivos-tree.txt: la lista de ficheros: archivos-tree.txt: the list of files from the tree package

lpic1-procesos.title: Finding, reprioritizing, and killing processes
lpic1-procesos.briefing:
In the system there are two processes that you did not launch, `copianocturna` and `minerocripto`, and a third program, `informe`, that is not running. The first two belong to `root` (use `sudo` where needed):
1. Find the PID of `copianocturna` and save it in `pid.txt` (just the number).
2. Change its nice value to 15 without stopping it.
3. Terminate `minerocripto` with `kill` and its default signal (SIGTERM).
4. Launch `informe 3600` in the background with nice value 10, so that it stays alive even if the terminal closes.
To check status: `ps -o pid,ni,comm -C copianocturna,minerocripto,informe`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-procesos`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-procesos.blind_alert: INCIDENT [PROCESSES] · A suspicious process is consuming resources and another one doing copies needs lower priority; there is also a heavy report to launch carefully.
hints: There are different tools for searching by name, for changing the priority of a process that is already running, and for launching a new one with different priority; `root` processes require privileges.

`pgrep -x NOMBRE` gives the PID; `renice -n VALOR -p PID` changes the priority of a running one; `kill PID` sends SIGTERM; `nohup nice -n VALOR comando &` launches it in the background immune to terminal closure.
`pgrep -x copianocturna > pid.txt`; `sudo renice -n 15 -p "$(cat pid.txt)"`; `sudo kill "$(pgrep -x minerocripto)"`; `nohup nice -n 10 informe 3600 >/dev/null 2>&1 &`.
lpic1-procesos.solution_summary: `pgrep -x` locates the PID by exact name, `renice -n 15 -p PID` re-prioritizes a live process, and `kill PID` terminates it with SIGTERM. To launch a new one with different priority and survive terminal closure, combine `nohup nice -n 10 comando &`.

checks.pid.txt tiene el PID de copianocturna: pid.txt contains the PID of copianocturna
checks.copianocturna sigue en marcha con nice 1: copianocturna is still running with nice 15

lpic1-find.title: Warehouse cleanup with find
lpic1-find.briefing:
The `almacen` folder contains files and directories of all kinds. Work from the challenge directory and use `find` with `almacen` as the starting point (paths must begin with `almacen/`):
1. Save in `grandes.txt` the paths of regular files larger than 2 MiB (one per line).
2. Save in `viejos.txt` the paths of regular files modified more than 365 days ago.
3. Remove write permission for “others” from all files that have it, using `find` with `-exec chmod`, without changing any other permission.
4. Delete with `find` all empty directories in `almacen`; any that contain something are kept.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-find`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-find.blind_alert: REQUEST [WAREHOUSE] · A folder needs an inventory of heavy and old files, open write permissions must be closed, and empty directories removed.
hints: `find` filters by type, size, age, permissions, and emptiness, and can act on what it finds. Watch the units of `-size` and note that exactly 2 MiB is not “more than 2 MiB”.
`-type f -size +2M`; `-type f -mtime +365`; `-type f -perm -o+w -exec chmod o-w {} \;`; `-type d -empty -delete`. The first two are redirected to a file.
`find almacen -type f -size +2M > grandes.txt`; `find almacen -type f -mtime +365 > viejos.txt`; `find almacen -type f -perm -o+w -exec chmod o-w {} \;`; `find almacen -type d -empty -delete`.
lpic1-find.solution_summary: `-size +2M` and `-mtime +365` select by size and age; `-perm -o+w` finds what is writable by “others” and `-exec chmod o-w {} \;` corrects it without touching anything else; `-type d -empty -delete` deletes empty directories (nested empty ones are removed from the inside out).

checks.grandes.txt: los ficheros de más de 2 Mi: grandes.txt: the files larger than 2 MiB (and nothing else)
checks.viejos.txt: los ficheros de más de un añ: viejos.txt: the files older than one year (and nothing else)
checks.ningún fichero es escribible por «otros»: no file is writable by “others” and all other permissions remain the same
checks.no quedan directorios vacíos y los que t: no empty directories remain and those that had something are kept

lpic1-vi.title: Editing a configuration file with vi
lpic1-vi.briefing:
Open `tienda.conf` with `vi` and leave it like this, without touching anything else:
1. Delete the line `depurar=si`.
2. Replace the word `tienda` with `almacen` throughout the file (comments included).
3. Duplicate the line `puerto=8080` just below it and, in the copy, change `puerto` to `puerto_admin` (result is `puerto_admin=8080`; the original remains the same).
4. Add `# editado con vi` as the first line of the file and `activo=si` as the last.
Save and exit the editor.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-vi`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-vi.blind_alert: REQUEST [EDITING] · A configuration file needs to be touched up from the terminal with the vi editor.
hints: `vi` has normal mode (movement, delete, copy, paste) and insert mode; commands starting with `:` (command line) handle substitution, saving, and quitting.

In normal mode: `dd` deletes a line, `yy` and `p` copy and paste, `cw` changes a word, `gg` and `G` jump to the beginning and end, `O` and `o` open a line above and below. With `:%s/viejo/nuevo/g` you substitute throughout the file; `:wq` saves and exits.

lpic1-vi.solution_summary: In normal mode `dd` deletes the line and `yy`+`p` duplicates it; `:%s/tienda/almacen/g` substitutes throughout the file; `gg O` and `G o` add lines at the beginning and end; `:wq` saves and exits. The result must be exactly the expected file, with no other changes.

lpic1-entorno-shell.title: An exported variable and a file with spaces in its name
lpic1-entorno-shell.briefing:
You are asked for two basic shell checks:
1. Define the variable `CURSO` with the text `LPIC 101` (including the space) and export it.
2. Launch a child `bash` that writes the value of `CURSO` to `hijo.txt`; that file must contain only `LPIC 101`.
3. Create an empty file named `notas de clase.txt`, with spaces inside the name (a single file).
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-entorno-shell`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-entorno-shell.blind_alert: REQUEST [ENVIRONMENT] · A value containing spaces must be passed to a child process, and a file whose name contains spaces must be created.
hints: A value with spaces needs quotes when assigning it, and a file name with spaces also needs them when using it, or the shell will split it into several words.
`export` so the child receives it; `bash -c 'printf "%s\n" "$CURSO"'` prints it from the child (with single quotes, so the child expands it). `touch` creates the empty file.
`CURSO="LPIC 101"; export CURSO`; `bash -c 'printf "%s\n" "$CURSO"' > hijo.txt`; `touch "notas de clase.txt"`.
lpic1-entorno-shell.solution_summary: Quotes prevent the shell from splitting words both in the value (`CURSO="LPIC 101"`) and in the file name. Only exported variables reach child processes, which is why they can print it.

lpic1-esquema-particionado.title: MBR partition scheme on an image and its fstab
lpic1-esquema-particionado.briefing:
You are asked to design the partitioning of a 1 GiB disk onto an image and write its `fstab` (none of this touches real disks; `sfdisk` is in `/usr/sbin`, use `sudo sfdisk`):
1. Create a raw disk image of exactly 1 GiB named `disco.img`.
2. Partition it with `sfdisk` using MBR table (`dos`) and 4 primary partitions: partition 1 of 200M type `83` (Linux, for `/boot`); partition 2 of 256M type `82` (swap); partition 3 of 300M type `83` (for `/`); and partition 4 with the remaining space, type `83` (for `/var`).
3. Create `fstab.nuevo` with a six-column line for each partition, as if they were `/dev/sdb1` through `/dev/sdb4`: `/boot`, swap (mount point `none`), `/` and `/var`, with filesystem type `ext4` (and `swap` for partition 2), options `defaults` (and `sw` for swap), dump `0` for all, and `fsck` order 1 for `/`, 2 for `/boot` and `/var`, and 0 for swap. The file must pass `findmnt --verify --tab-file fstab.nuevo` without errors.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-esquema-particionado`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-esquema-particionado.blind_alert: REQUEST [STORAGE] · The layout of a new disk must be designed and its mount table written up before installation.
hints: An image is a file the size of a disk; `sfdisk` reads its partition description from standard input. An `fstab` has six columns: device, mount point, type, options, dump, and pass.

`truncate -s 1G disco.img`; to `sudo sfdisk disco.img` you pass `label: dos` and one `size=…, type=…` line per partition (the last one without `size` takes the rest). To validate the `fstab`, `findmnt --verify --tab-file`.

`truncate -s 1G disco.img`; `sudo sfdisk disco.img` with `label: dos`, `size=200M, type=83`, `size=256M, type=82`, `size=300M, type=83`, `type=83`; in `fstab.nuevo`: `/dev/sdb1 /boot ext4 defaults 0 2`, `/dev/sdb2 none swap sw 0 0`, `/dev/sdb3 / ext4 defaults 0 1`, `/dev/sdb4 /var ext4 defaults 0 2`.
lpic1-esquema-particionado.solution_summary: `truncate -s 1G` creates the image; `sfdisk` receives the table as text (`label: dos` and one `size=, type=` line per partition, the last one with no size). The `fstab` has six columns: root with pass 1, `/boot` and `/var` with pass 2, and swap as `none swap sw 0 0`; `findmnt --verify` validates it.

checks.disco.img existe y tiene un tamaño de 1: disco.img exists and is 1 GiB in size
checks.disco.img tiene tabla MBR con 4 particio: disco.img has an MBR table with 4 partitions (/boot, swap, /, /var)
checks.fstab.nuevo es sintácticamente válido se: fstab.nuevo is syntactically valid according to findmnt

lpic1-hardware.title: Kernel modules, blacklisting, and processor data
lpic1-hardware.briefing:
You are asked for four hardware adjustments (files under `/etc` require privileges: use `sudo` to write them):
1. Save to `modulos.txt` the list of kernel-loaded modules exactly as shown by `lsmod`.
2. Create `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-audio.conf` with the directive that prevents automatic loading of the `snd_hda_intel` module.
3. Extract from `/proc/cpuinfo` the processor model name value (what comes after `model name :`, without the prefix) and save it in `cpu-modelo.txt`, on a single line.
4. Create `/etc/modules-load.d/red-virtual.conf` so that the `dummy` module loads at system boot.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-hardware`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-hardware.blind_alert: REQUEST [HARDWARE] · The state of the modules must be recorded, an audio driver blacklisted, a virtual network module loaded at boot, and the CPU documented.
hints: Loaded modules come from `/proc/modules`, the processor model from `/proc/cpuinfo`, and files in `/etc/modprobe.d/` and `/etc/modules-load.d/` are text lists with one directive or module per line.

`lsmod > modulos.txt`; `grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo` and `sed` to remove the prefix; in `modprobe.d` the keyword is the blacklist one; in `modules-load.d` the module name is enough. Write to `/etc` with `sudo tee`.

`lsmod > modulos.txt`; `echo 'blacklist snd_hda_intel' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-audio.conf`; `grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/.*: //' > cpu-modelo.txt`; `echo dummy | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/red-virtual.conf`.

lpic1-variables-entorno.title: Local and exported variables, and the literal $
lpic1-variables-entorno.briefing:
You are asked to demonstrate the difference between a shell variable and an environment variable:
1. Create the variable `VAR_LOCAL` with the value `solo aqui` without exporting it, and `VAR_EXPORTADA` with the value `hola desde el padre`, this one exported.
2. Launch a child `bash` that writes, each on its own line and in brackets, the value of `VAR_LOCAL` and `VAR_EXPORTADA`, and save its output to `hijos.txt`. It must be exactly `[]` and, below it, `[hola desde el padre]`.
3. Save to `env.txt` only the lines of `env` output that start with `VAR_`, and to `printenv.txt` the value of `VAR_EXPORTADA` obtained with `printenv` (just the value).
4. Remove `VAR_EXPORTADA` from the shell and save to `unset.txt` the attempt to print it in brackets: it must be `[]`.
5. Create `comillas.txt` with two lines containing the literal text `$HOME` (without expanding): the first written with single quotes and the second with double quotes escaping the `$`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-variables-entorno`); files requested without a path go there. Do steps 1 through 4 in the same shell, because variables live there.
lpic1-variables-entorno.blind_alert: REQUEST [ENVIRONMENT] · It must be demonstrated which shell variables child processes inherit and how to write a literal `$`.
hints: An unexported variable only exists in the shell that created it; child processes inherit only exported ones. Between `$` and quotes the difference is who expands what.

`export` marks the variable for children; `bash -c '…'` creates the child (with single quotes the `$` is expanded by the child, not your shell). `unset` removes a variable and `${VAR-}` expands to empty if it does not exist. In single quotes the `$` is literal; in double quotes, escape it with a backslash.

`VAR_LOCAL="solo aqui"; export VAR_EXPORTADA="hola desde el padre"`; `bash -c 'echo "[$VAR_LOCAL]"; echo "[$VAR_EXPORTADA]"' > hijos.txt`; `env | grep '^VAR_' > env.txt`; `printenv VAR_EXPORTADA > printenv.txt`; `unset VAR_EXPORTADA; echo "[${VAR_EXPORTADA-}]" > unset.txt`; `printf '%s\n' '$HOME' "\$HOME" > comillas.txt`.
lpic1-variables-entorno.solution_summary: The child shell inherits only variables exported with `export`, which is why it sees `VAR_EXPORTADA` and not `VAR_LOCAL`; `env` and `printenv` show only the exported environment. `unset` removes the variable and `${VAR-}` avoids an error by expanding it empty. With single quotes the `$` is literal, and with double quotes it must be escaped (`\$HOME`).

checks.env.txt: solo VAR_EXPORTADA, con su valo: env.txt: only VAR_EXPORTADA, with its value

lpic1-multiplexor-tmux.title: A tmux session driven from outside
lpic1-multiplexor-tmux.briefing:
You are asked to manage a `tmux` session without entering it:
1. Create a background session named `lpi101` that runs `bash` and whose starting directory is the challenge directory.
2. Save the list of `tmux` sessions to `sesiones.txt`.
3. Send the session `lpi101` the command `echo "hola desde tmux"` followed by Enter.
4. Wait one second and save to `pantalla.txt` the text shown in that session (text only, without entering it).
5. Close the `lpi101` session; it must not remain alive when finished.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-multiplexor-tmux`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-multiplexor-tmux.blind_alert: REQUEST [TERMINAL] · A persistent terminal session must be launched, typed into remotely, and its output captured.
hints: `tmux` can create, write to, and read a session without you being inside; each action is a subcommand with the target session option.

`new-session` with the options for background, name, and directory; `ls` to list; `send-keys -t NOMBRE 'texto' Enter`; `capture-pane` with the option that prints to standard output; `kill-session -t NOMBRE`. Pause with `sleep 1` before capturing.

`tmux new-session -d -s lpi101 -c "$PWD" bash`; `tmux ls > sesiones.txt`; `tmux send-keys -t lpi101 'echo "hola desde tmux"' Enter`; `sleep 1; tmux capture-pane -p -t lpi101 > pantalla.txt`; `tmux kill-session -t lpi101`.
lpic1-multiplexor-tmux.solution_summary: `new-session -d -s NOMBRE -c DIR` creates the detached session, `send-keys` types into it, and `capture-pane -p` dumps the screen to standard output; wait a moment for the command to execute. `kill-session -t NOMBRE` closes it at the end.

lpic1-dependencias.title: Bash shared libraries
lpic1-dependencias.briefing:
You are asked to document the libraries of `/bin/bash` (`ldconfig` is in `/usr/sbin`, which is not in your PATH: use `sudo ldconfig` or `/usr/sbin/ldconfig`):
1. Save to `bash-dependencias.txt` the shared libraries needed by `/bin/bash`.
2. Extract from that file only the `libc.so.6` line and save it to `glibc.txt`.
3. Search the dynamic linker cache (`ldconfig`) for the `libc.so.6` entry and save it to `cache-glibc.txt`.
Your terminal opens in the challenge directory (`/home/alumno/retos/r101-dependencias`); files requested without a path go there.
lpic1-dependencias.blind_alert: REQUEST [LIBRARIES] · It must be documented which shared libraries Bash depends on and where the system locates them.
hints: There is a command that shows which libraries an executable depends on and another that shows the system’s library cache; the rest is filtering with `grep`.
`ldd RUTA` lists dependencies; `sudo ldconfig -p` prints the cache; each result is filtered with `grep libc.so.6` and redirected to the requested file.
`ldd /bin/bash > bash-dependencias.txt`; `grep 'libc.so.6 =>' bash-dependencias.txt > glibc.txt`; `sudo ldconfig -p | grep 'libc.so.6' > cache-glibc.txt`.
lpic1-dependencias.solution_summary: `ldd` resolves the dynamic dependencies of a binary and `ldconfig -p` prints the library cache used by the linker; `grep` isolates the `libc.so.6` entry in both cases.
